subject: Biology
title: Circadian Rhythms in Animals
description: One-minute skill: Circadian Rhythms in Animals.

hook.text: Even in total darkness, a hamster will run on its wheel at the same time every day.

buildup.text: Circadian rhythms are internal clocks that cycle roughly every 24 hours.

discovery.text: A cluster of neurons in the brain called the SCN acts as the master clock in mammals.

twist.text: Jet lag happens because your clock and the environment are temporarily out of sync.

climax.text: Circadian rhythms control sleep, feeding, hormone release, and body temperature across the animal kingdom.

punchline.text: Every animal carries a clock it never needs to wind.

quiz.question: What is the SCN?
options: A light-sensing organ in the eye

details.summary: Circadian rhythms are internal biological clocks that cycle approximately every 24 hours, regulating sleep, feeding, hormone release, and activity patterns in virtually all animals. These clocks persist even without external cues like light and darkness.
details.whyItMatters: Circadian rhythms synchronize an animal's physiology and behavior with the day-night cycle. Disrupting these clocks in laboratory animals causes metabolic disorders, immune dysfunction, and reduced lifespan.
takeaways: Internal clocks run on roughly 24-hour cycles even in constant darkness
Light resets circadian clocks daily through photoreceptor pathways
Circadian disruption impairs health, cognition, and survival

faq.question: How do animals maintain circadian rhythms without light?
faq.answer: Molecular clock genes produce proteins that accumulate and degrade in a feedback loop lasting about 24 hours. This internal oscillator keeps running in total darkness, though it gradually drifts without light cues to reset it daily.

faq.question: Do nocturnal and diurnal animals have different clocks?
faq.answer: The core clock mechanism is similar, but downstream outputs differ. Nocturnal animals activate during the dark phase of the same 24-hour cycle. The molecular clockwork is conserved; what changes is which behaviors it activates at which phase.
